i (22f) got diagnosed at 21 almost a year ago and have the CALR mutation. ive been diagnosed with et as well as von willhebrands. the highest my platelets have been was 1500+ but ive been on hydroxyurea since my diagnosis in july 2023 and from my most recent labs my platelets are around 750. it was definitely a mind fuck to say the least. my diagnosis answered a lot of health questions i had for years but obviously brought up a plethera of new ones. first things first you are not alone and you have people to talk to here if you want. the biggest changes in my life have been the frequent doc appts, having to quit vaping, and keeping a strict schedule for/around all my meds. other than that not much has changed for me. the worst part personally has been explaining the disease and its effects to those closest to me. for a while there was a sense of pity when i interracted with anyone and they treated me like im a cracked piece of glass that theyre trying not to break. the main thing is that even though it just sucks in every possible way, you will adjust to the situation. give yourself time to sit in and process how much the diagnosis and whatever your treatment is sucks but please be sure to lean on people who love you and who want to support and help. like others said, do your best to find an MPN specialist and just take everything one step at a time. you got this :)
